executive_assessment.text: Saburai, Tapo-Memo, Gildapil, Lebos and RAEOA cases add named-site vulnerabilities; local resource disputes remain distinct from evidence of climate-caused conflict.
Tara bandu and spring protection, catchment works and early-warning handovers add concrete capacity, with historical citations, count inconsistencies and unmeasured persistence retained.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-02 reports: Participants reported rainy-season landslides and floods destroying farms in Saburai, Tapo-Memo, Gildapil and Lebos (Bobonaro); Gildapil participants described hunger after maize loss.
Source dated 2024-02 reports: In RAEOA, wet-season landslides in Bene-Ufe damaged roads, settlements and farms; flooding and landslides displaced 280 families around Nibin, Usitaqueno, in 2021.

Source dated 2024-02 reports: Communities reportedly protected 80 water resources in RAEOA; Usi Taqueno residents fenced and cleaned springs, while Saburai protected water distribution through tara bandu.

Source dated 2025-08 reports: The WASH climate assessment says all municipalities face flood exposure; the largest numbers exposed to extreme floods are in Bobonaro and Dili, followed by Ainaro and Baucau.

Source dated 2025-07-04 reports: UNICEF reports community catchment-management expansion to 35 additional sub-villages in Ainaro and Viqueque, implemented by 70 trained residents and nearly 350 other community members, including women and youth.

Source dated 2025-07-04 reports: The 532 built nature-based structures (45 ponds, 313 terraces and 174 check dams) were reported to retain at least 12,567 m³ in one rainfall event; dry-season replenishment is expected, not measured.

Source dated 2024-03-27 reports: Sixteen early-warning devices were handed to DNMG; disaster committees were supported in Dili sucos. The article says 15 PREPARADU sucos but lists 16, including six Maloa sites: Villa Verde, Motael, Colmera, Campo Alor, Bairo Pite and Dare.

The June 2024 EU/Mercy Corps close-out account reports 537 households with improved shock-preparation capacity, 1,284 people with climate-resilience knowledge and 68 mitigation/adaptation works in the Maloa watershed.

known_gaps.text: No countrywide causal estimate of climate impacts on conflict or violence is established by these sources.
Full subnational coverage and independently evaluated long-term response effectiveness remain gaps.
A climate-peacebuilding PDF could not be retrieved; no resource-conflict claim is imported from its search snippet.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.

The 2026 UNICEF CCRI-DRM narrative does not expose named-municipality scores in accessible text, and its companion geospatial platform could not be accessed; no rankings from secondary summaries were used.
The border-community study is qualitative and based on selected villages; its reported resource disputes are not attributed to climate change.
The climate/WASH assessment combines varying data vintages and cites 2017 ACAPS material for water disputes; it is not a current conflict or violence assessment.
No inspected source shows insecurity or violence directly blocking a named climate-adaptation project; disaster-related access interruption is documented but is not a reverse FCV-to-climate finding.
UNICEF and project close-out results are implementer-reported; expected water replenishment and broader resilience or peace effects were not independently evaluated.
TATOLI says 15 PREPARADU sucos were supported but enumerates 16; the count was not reconciled.

Main verified the border assessment's named Malibaka case and 2021 280-family displacement, the WASH report's dated citation, and the EU close-out body. Climate effects are not assigned to border disputes.
Main directly reopened the EU close-out paragraphs containing the 537-household, 1,284-person and 68-works figures. These remain implementer-reported, not causal impact estimates.
